persistence_invariants.brief: A UNIQUE constraint on (sku, location) rejects a second row for the same pair at the DB, so two stored duplicates can never exist (R3).
sku is NOT NULL: inserting a row with a null sku is rejected by the DB.
location is NOT NULL: inserting a row with a null location is rejected by the DB.
tracking_code is NOT NULL: inserting a row with a null tracking_code is rejected by the DB.
quantity is NOT NULL: inserting a row with a null quantity is rejected by the DB.
CHECK (quantity >= 0) rejects a negative quantity at the DB, so a stored negative stock level is impossible (R2).
CHECK (par_level IS NULL OR par_level >= 0): par_level is nullable (absent = not tracked) but never negative.
CHECK (batch IS NULL OR batch <> '') AND (serial IS NULL OR serial <> ''): an absent optional detail is NULL, never an empty string (AC3, R9).
Filing is a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (sku, location) DO UPDATE in one transaction: a re-file updates the one existing row in place, and a rejected write leaves the table unchanged.

Initial create_table: after downgrade to the migration's down_revision then upgrade head, stock_records and its columns, unique and check constraints are present again (schema recreated; no data-survival claim for the initial creation).

stock_adjustments.stock_record_id is NOT NULL and REFERENCES stock_records(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT: an adjustment for a nonexistent record is rejected, and a stock record with audit history cannot be silently deleted out from under its trail.
actor is NOT NULL: inserting an adjustment with a null actor is rejected by the DB (R1).
created_at is NOT NULL with a server DEFAULT now(): every adjustment carries a DB-assigned timestamp, never a client-supplied or missing one (R1).
quantity_before and quantity_after are NOT NULL: inserting an adjustment missing either is rejected by the DB.
CHECK (btrim(actor) <> ''): a blank or whitespace-only actor is rejected at the DB (AC3 defense in depth).
CHECK (quantity_before >= 0 AND quantity_after >= 0): an audit entry can never record a negative stock level (R2).

A BEFORE UPDATE trigger on stock_adjustments raises, so a direct UPDATE of any entry's timestamp, actor or quantities is refused at the DB and the row stays exactly as recorded (R1, AC5). DELETE is refused at the API (no delete route); the DB leaves DELETE open only so FK-aware test cleanup can run.

An adjustment locks the stock_records row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), updates its quantity and inserts the stock_adjustments entry (quantity_before = prior stored value) in ONE transaction: a rejected adjustment leaves both stock_records and stock_adjustments unchanged, and an accepted one never updates quantity without its audit entry.

Additive migration on pre-existing stock_records: upgrade creates stock_adjustments without altering stock_records; downgrade to its down_revision drops only stock_adjustments and every pre-existing stock_records row survives unchanged; upgrade head recreates stock_adjustments with its FK, checks and trigger (R1, R8).

access_patterns.brief: Equality lookup WHERE tracking_code = :code ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1 for scan-to-screen under ~200ms (R6); non-unique btree index candidate.

Equality filter WHERE sku = :sku ORDER BY location for the SKU detail view; likely served by the leading column of the (sku, location) unique index (PI1), so the DBA may record a deliberate no-new-index decision.
Equality filter WHERE stock_record_id = :id ORDER BY created_at, id for the adjustment history panel (AC4); composite btree index candidate (also serves the FK).

api_contracts.item: Request JSON {sku: string, location: string, tracking_code: string, quantity: int>=0, par_level: int|null, batch: string|null, serial: string|null} (blank optional strings normalized to null by the service). Success: 201 when a new (sku, location) is filed, 200 when an existing pair is updated in place; body {outcome: 'filed'|'updated', record: {id: int, sku: string, location: string, tracking_code: string, quantity: int, par_level: int|null, batch: string|null, serial: string|null, created_at: ISO-8601, updated_at: ISO-8601}}. Validation failure: 422 with body {errors: [{field: 'sku'|'location'|'tracking_code'|'quantity'|'par_level', message: string naming the field}]}; no row created or changed.

200: {record: {id: int, sku: string, location: string, tracking_code: string, quantity: int, par_level: int|null, batch: string|null, serial: string|null, created_at: ISO-8601, updated_at: ISO-8601}} for the most recently updated row whose tracking_code equals code. 404: {detail: string, code: string} when no row matches (client renders lookup-not-found, never an error page). 422 {errors:[{field:'code', message}]} when code is blank.

200: bare JSON array of stock records {id: int, sku: string, location: string, tracking_code: string, quantity: int, par_level: int|null, batch: string|null, serial: string|null, created_at: ISO-8601, updated_at: ISO-8601}, one per (sku, location), ordered by sku then location; [] when no rows exist (client renders stock-empty).

200: bare JSON array of the stock records {id: int, sku: string, location: string, tracking_code: string, quantity: int, par_level: int|null, batch: string|null, serial: string|null, created_at: ISO-8601, updated_at: ISO-8601} whose sku equals the path sku, ordered by location; [] when the SKU has no records (client renders sku-not-found).

Request JSON {quantity: int (the NEW absolute quantity, >= 0), actor: string (operator-typed, required, no auth)}. 200: {record: {id: int, sku: string, location: string, tracking_code: string, quantity: int, par_level: int|null, batch: string|null, serial: string|null, created_at: ISO-8601, updated_at: ISO-8601}, adjustment: {id: int, stock_record_id: int, actor: string, quantity_before: int, quantity_after: int, created_at: ISO-8601 (server-assigned)}}; record.quantity is the stored value the client reconciles its optimistic row to. 422: {errors: [{field: 'quantity'|'actor', message: string naming the field}]} when quantity < 0 / missing or actor blank; nothing written. 404 {detail: string} when the record id does not exist.

200: bare JSON array of {id: int, stock_record_id: int, actor: string, quantity_before: int, quantity_after: int, created_at: ISO-8601 (server-assigned)} for that record, ordered by created_at then id ascending (time order); [] when none (client renders history-empty). 404 {detail} when the record id does not exist.
Always 405 {detail: string} (PUT and PATCH on the same path also 405 {detail}); no route mutates or deletes an audit entry, and the entry is unchanged afterwards.

open_decisions.question: Where is the immutable timestamp + caller-supplied actor (no auth in V1) for each inventory adjustment stored (separate stock_movements table vs columns on stock_records)? S1 filing records only created_at/updated_at.
open_decisions.resolution: A separate append-only stock_adjustments table (FK stock_record_id, actor typed by the operator — no auth in V1 — server created_at, quantity_before/after), written atomically with the stock_records quantity update (PI18). S1 filing/re-file does NOT write an adjustment entry, so gated S1 ACs are unaffected; stock_records stays the one row per (sku, location).

open_decisions.question: The R2 no-overcommit rule needs a pick/allocation operation, which F1 does not introduce; which feature/story owns it?
Is tracking_code unique across stock_records (one record per code) or may several (sku, location) rows share a code for find-by-tracking-code?
open_decisions.resolution: tracking_code is NOT unique (no DB unique constraint; S1 filing never rejects a shared code, so adding one would contradict gated S1 AC1/AC2). Lookup returns the single most recently updated matching row (EP2), indexed by AP1.

open_decisions.question: How does the API distinguish a new filing from a re-file?
open_decisions.resolution: 201 + outcome 'filed' for a new pair, 200 + outcome 'updated' for an in-place re-file (EP1-file-stock-record).

open_decisions.question: Should an S1 re-file that changes quantity (EP1 'updated') also append a stock_adjustments entry, or does the audit trail cover only explicit adjustments?
